A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm has been asking about the strange leaves all week — "but what IS it?" Tonight, an answer. Aitana drew a towering emergent tree with a buttressed trunk, dropping pods full of silky fiber and dark seeds in the dirt for the others. It'll wash away. The knowledge won't.

A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm spends the afternoon with the thorny bush with dark berries — look, smell, the smallest taste, then waiting. An hour passes. Then another. Nothing. The fire nods. That's dinner, maybe.
💡 You see it again in your mind: a thorny bush with dark berries. A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm's words land on the memory like a label. Blackberry. Of course.
A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm came back with 367 kcal of something edible. The pantry can't take it all — 184 kcal in, 183 kcal eaten at the fire.

You catch fragments by the fire — Na telling A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm about Susan. The truth left this story two fires ago. What's left is better theater.

A woman, maybe 30s, with a burn-scarred forearm leans in, voice low. "Here's what we figured out about the thing with headlights for eyes, standing too still. MOVE, don't stare. When it goes still, the beam is coming — MOVE, don't stare at the light. Anything beats standing there: the freeze means it is already aiming."
★ IDENTIFIED: European Elder. Elder. Big shrub; flat white flower plates in June, drooping black berry clusters in late summer. Uses unknown — harvest, taste, and learn.
